newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Italy's Ciampi favours strong EU institutions.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi favours strong EU institutions.

text.p: Italian Finance Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Monday he favoured a strengthening of existing EU institutions to counter-balance the power of a European central bank.
"In the face of a European central bank you need a balance of political power just like in the nation states," Ciampi told a news conference after a meeting of EU Finance Ministers.
But Ciampi also said he was in favour of giving more power to existing institutions, such as the European Council and the Council of Finance Ministers.

Ciampi also said that Italy backed the timetable and the criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) laid down in the Maastricht Treaty but also shared France's emphasis on the need for job creation.

"We all agree on the objectives, timing and criteria of Maastricht. There are no differences. The train has left and cannot stop. There is no will on anybody's part to renegotiate, not even on the part of the French," said Ciampi.
France earlier asked for time to study a previously agreed "stability pact" to keep budget deficits tight after the single European currency is launched.
Ciampi said he did not rule out a further meeting of EU Finance Ministers before the Amsterdam summit of EU leaders on June 16-17.
